newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam bank official says violations increasing.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam bank official says violations increasing.

text.p: Vietnam's State Bank Governor Cao Si Kiem has warned that violations within the country's banking system are increasing despite strict measures to tackle the problem, state media said on Wednesday.

The Nhan Dan and Quan Doi Nhan Dan newspapers quoted Kiem as saying in a speech to the National Assembly that checks by state inspectors showed 21.7 billion dong ($1.96 million) had been lost to corrupt officials in commercial banks.
The period of the losses was not given, but he said 1,600 bank workers had been disciplined over the past four years for various violations.
"Though many strict measures have been worked out to deal with this, the number of violations in the banking system keeps increasing," Kiem said.
He added that losses in the banking system from bad debts from two major corruption cases totalled more than $54 million.
"Since 1994, we have inspected comprehensively and punished many cadres. But because of a lack of determination and coordination, the work has not been very efficient," he said.
"In general, the banking system has allowed big losses but only a part of that has been recovered."
Vietnam's banking system has recently come under attack in the country's state-controlled media.

Last month a blunt editorial in the Nhan Dan newspaper, a mouthpiece of the ruling Communist Party, accused the banks of incompetence and corruption, and that millions of dollars risked being lost through poor management of debt.
The newspaper said 4.2 percent of the debt owed to state-owned commercial banks was overdue.
Among private banks the figure for overdue debt was 5.2 percent, but the report said the quality of debt meant as much as 50 percent of this may never be recovered. (US$1=VND 11,065)
